references.name: text-embeddings-inference
references.procedure: POST /decode then /tokenize to check the rows survive TEI's re-tokenization; then POST /embed with the batch's 32 rows as token ids, 5 untimed then 50 timed, each timed from sending the request to reading the whole response, the p50 and p99 of TEI's x-total-time, x-tokenization-time, x-queue-time, x-inference-time headers beside it, and TEI's /metrics read before and after the timed requests for its te_batch_next_size and te_batch_next_tokens histograms; min_cosine is against the bundle's reference vectors; TEI's router built natively and run on this machine, not in a container; round trip (measured) p50 1517.538 ms, p99 1925.952 ms; TEI's own headers, whole ms, over the same requests: x-total-time p50 1513 p99 1923, x-tokenization-time p50 2 p99 5, x-queue-time p50 242 p99 444, x-inference-time p50 1106 p99 1664; TEI's /metrics over the timed requests: 1600 inputs in 50 requests, 148 backend batches (te_batch_next_size's 270 samples less the 122 empty polls te_batch_next_tokens shows), 2.96 batches per request, mean batch size 10.81 inputs (batches by size, 1: 28, 2: 15, 3 to 4: 29, 5 to 8: 19, 9 to 16: 9, 17 to 32: 48); the tool ran unpinned; TEI ran unpinned with the image's thread settings: OMP_NUM_THREADS=unset, MKL_NUM_THREADS=unset, RAYON_NUM_THREADS=unset

references.name: mlx
references.procedure: MLX 0.29.3 on the machine's Python, the BERT encoder of bench/reference/mlx_reference.py with every weight cast to float16, mx.compile, mean pooling and L2 in F32, on the same token rows as a padded batch; untimed runs, then 50 timed from the host, each waited for with mx.eval. min_cosine is against each row's expected vector.
